summaries.summary: This community centers on hardware products—notably the Borealis controller built at the Brno plant and the Meridian flow meter assembled at Tartu under Elin Saar—and their supporting telemetry infrastructure. Production and deployments to clients like Pellham Labs, Varnell Bay Marina, and Northmoor Irrigation District rely heavily on key suppliers, including Kerrin Sensors and Varnell Semiconductor. Critical operational risks have surfaced over time, evidenced by a March 2026 six-week QX-7 radio chip shipment delay from sole-supplier Varnell (prompting Kerrin Sensors to qualify as a second source) and a May 2026 Telemetry Gateway outage that disrupted device uploads. Organizational changes over time include the Telemetry Gateway transitioning to Ana Duarte's Data Platform team in September 2026, alongside hardware upgrades such as the PM-2 power module replacing the older PM-1.

The Hardware team, led by Tomas Berg, owns the Atlas-3 sensor, which is deployed across clients including Brightwater Aquaculture, Calder Grain Co-op, and Osterby Water Utility—the latter two managed by Lena Vik, with Osterby's deployment expanding over time from 420 to 510 units. A key hardware dependency changed starting with the May build, when Sundra Power's Sundra C2 cell replaced Hallam Cells' LX-4 lithium cell as the Atlas-3's power source. This component transition introduces operational and compatibility risks across both existing and incoming Atlas-3 deployments.

Priya Raman leads the Firmware team, establishing a direct leadership dependency for the group's initiatives. The Firmware team is responsible for owning and maintaining critical infrastructure, specifically the OTA Update Service and the Telemetry Gateway. No explicit risks or historical changes over time are detailed in the provided facts.
